question: What did J. M. E. McTaggart's 1908 paper, source of the A-series and B-series, set out to prove?
options: That time flows at one rate
answer: That time is unreal. McTaggart held that change needs the A-series, events being past, present or future, but that every event would then have to be all three, a contradiction; the B-series of earlier and later alone gives no change. His conclusion won few converts, yet his two labels still organise the debate.
move: An argument's vocabulary can outlive its conclusion by a century.
trap: Linking his past-present-future series with the view that only now exists.
reference: McTaggart, The Unreality of Time, Mind 17 (68), 1908, pp. 457-474
